english.title: Affray
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used or threatened unlawful violence towards

(A)_[another]_
(B)_[other persons]_

and your conduct was such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3(1) and (7) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used/threatened unlawful violence towards another
and his/her conduct was such as would cause
a person of reasonable firmness to fear for personal safety

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A threat under this section cannot be made by words alone.
(ii) Where more persons have used or threatened unlawful violence etc (as above) than are charged, option (B) should always be used. See R v Mahroof (1989) at C119.
(iii) See the CPS charging standards for this offence before preparing any charges.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Three years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
